card.intuition: A token is the atomic unit a model reads and writes — roughly word-sized, but common words are one token while rare or long ones split into several via a fixed tokenizer vocabulary. Context window size, cost, and latency are all counted in tokens, roughly three-quarters of an English word each.
card.analogy: Tokens are like metered postage measured in ounces rather than boxes: a dense all-caps printout is heavy even when it looks small, and both shipping cost and package-size limits are quoted in the same ounce unit.
card.time_complexity: Latency and cost scale with token count: output is generated one token at a time (tokens per second), and you are billed separately for input and output tokens on every model provider request.
card.space_complexity: The context window is a fixed number of tokens — a small file full of unusual strings (hashes, base64 blobs, minified code) can eat surprising amounts of it.
when_to_use: Estimating prompt cost and context usage before sending large content into a session
Comparing model tiers by tokens-per-dollar and tokens-per-second
Reasoning about context-window filling and when to hand off or compact
gotchas: Token boundaries do not match word boundaries — never say 'word' when you mean 'token'
Code tokenizes unpredictably: keywords are cheap, hashes and generated identifiers are expensive

steps.label: Text
steps.annotation: Raw input text arrives at the tokenizer.

steps.label: Split
steps.annotation: The tokenizer cuts text into fragments from a fixed vocabulary.

steps.label: Encode
steps.annotation: The model sees only token ids, never characters or words.

steps.label: Predict
steps.annotation: The model predicts the next token, appends it, and repeats.

steps.label: Count
steps.annotation: Context, cost, and latency are all measured in tokens.

exercise.prompt: Token costs depend on content: unusual strings split into more tokens than plain words. Count tokens, adding a surcharge for every non-alphabetic fragment.
exercise.starter_code:
def count_tokens(text):
    tokens = text.split()
    extra = sum(1 for t in tokens if not t.isalpha())
    return len(___________) + extra
hints: Every whitespace-separated chunk is one base token
The extra surcharge counts fragments that contain digits or symbols
exercise.test_code:
assert count_tokens("a3f9c2 e1") == 4
assert count_tokens("def print x") == 3
